title: Surface code quantum computing by lattice surgery
authors: Dominic Horsman; Austin G. Fowler; Simon Devitt; Rodney Van Meter
supports: New J. Phys. 14, 123011 (2012). Lattice surgery by merging and splitting planar patches; rough merge measures X_L X_L (strip in |0>), smooth merge measures Z_L Z_L (strip in |+>), each with d rounds of error correction; CNOT via an intermediate |+>_L patch, reducible to d rounds; 53-qubit distance-3 lattice-surgery CNOT; corrections applied by reinterpreting later outcomes.

title: A Game of Surface Codes: Large-Scale Quantum Computing with Lattice Surgery
supports: Quantum 3, 128 (2019). Pauli product measurements via lattice surgery in about d code cycles; Clifford gates commuted to the end and absorbed into measurements; magic state consumed via P⊗Z measurement with P_{π/4} correction on -1 and Pauli correction after X measurement; controlled-Pauli gates from a |+> ancilla and Pauli product measurements (Fig. 33b); compact block 1.5n+3 tiles; time-optimal scheme runs n_L T layers in n_L·t_m; 10^8 T gates in 10 s at 10 µs feed-forward.
note: The 10-second example assumes 10^8 T gates arranged in 10^6 layers of 100. A Toffoli costs 7 π/8 rotations, or 4 T gates with a cheaper construction (Sec. 6).

title: On Universal and Fault-Tolerant Quantum Computing
authors: P. Oscar Boykin; Tal Mor; Matthew Pulver; Vwani Roychowdhury; Farrokh Vatan
supports: arXiv quant-ph/9906054 (1999). Hadamard, σz^{1/4} (the T gate up to phase) and CNOT form a universal fault-tolerant basis; CNOT and Hadamard alone are not universal.
note: Journal version not checked; cited by its arXiv identifier.

title: Restrictions on Transversal Encoded Quantum Gate Sets
supports: Phys. Rev. Lett. 102, 110502 (2009). A code that detects arbitrary errors on any single physical subsystem cannot have a universal transversal encoded gate set.

title: Classification of topologically protected gates for local stabilizer codes
supports: Phys. Rev. Lett. 110, 170503 (2013). For 2D topological stabilizer codes, logical gates implementable by constant-depth circuits are restricted to the Clifford group.

title: Universal quantum computation with ideal Clifford gates and noisy ancillas
supports: Phys. Rev. A 71, 022316 (2005). Clifford operations plus noisy magic states give universality via distillation; 15-to-1 protocol distilling |A0>=(|0>+e^{iπ/4}|1>)/√2 with success probability (1+15(1-2ε)^8)/16 (Eq. 35), exact output error (Eq. 36), threshold ε0≈0.141 (Eq. 37), ε_out≈35ε^3 (Eq. 38), recursion (1/√35)(√35 ε)^{3^k}.

title: Magic State Distillation: Not as Costly as You Think
supports: Quantum 3, 205 (2019). Table 1: at p=1e-3, (15-to-1)_{17,7,7} gives 4.5e-8 with 4,620 qubits and 42.6 cycles; (15-to-1)^6_{13,5,5}×(20-to-4)_{23,11,13} gives 1.4e-10 with 43,300 qubits and 130 cycles; (15-to-1)^6_{17,7,7}×(15-to-1)_{41,17,17} gives 4.5e-20 with 73,400 qubits and 128 cycles; historical designs up to 800,000 qubits. Origin of 35p^3 (35 undetected weight-3 fault combinations; exact 3.501e-11 at p=1e-4). About 10% of qubits for distillation in a 100-qubit example at p=1e-3.
note: Table 1 qubits and cycles are per protocol run; for multi-output protocols (e.g. 20-to-4) the space-time cost and output error are per magic state.

title: Magic state cultivation: growing T states as cheap as CNOT gates
authors: Craig Gidney; Noah Shutty; Cody Jones
supports: arXiv preprint 2409.17595 (2024). Cultivation fits in one surface-code patch, uses roughly the gate count of a lattice-surgery CNOT of equivalent reliability and an order of magnitude fewer qubit-rounds than prior work; simulated logical error about 2e-9 at 1e-3 noise and 4e-11 at 5e-4; Figure 2 lists a 99% end-to-end discard rate for the 2e-9 case and Li 2015 injection at 5e-3 error.
note: Preprint; results are simulations, not hardware data.

title: How to factor 2048 bit RSA integers in 8 hours using 20 million noisy qubits (full-text details)
supports: Quantum 5, 433 (2021). Abstract formulas: 0.3n^3+0.0005n^3 lg n Toffolis and 500n^2+n^2 lg n measurement depth; definition of reaction time (trigger a logical measurement, collect and error-correct the result, choose the next basis); 14 CCZ factories needed for the reaction-limited rate at d=27; lookup addition about 37 ms of which about 22 ms reaction-limited; Table 2 single-factory row: 16 million qubits, 6 days.
note: Complements the existing abstract-level record dp-gidney-ekera-2021.
